svg.title: LOT and Silicon Labs Matter connectivity boundary
svg.desc: A conceptual boundary diagram showing the host CPU and LOT interconnect separated from the external connectivity device and Matter/IP network. SoC and NCP are alternative device modes, not simultaneously assumed.
svg.text: Where LOT ends and Matter connectivity begins
Conceptual boundary only — the actual Silicon Labs part, operating mode, and host interface are not yet selected.
HOST / LOT SIDE
CPU / host processor
Core and native bus must be identified
Reusable interconnect + LOT routing
Only select after bus / transaction contract is known
Host-side device interface
CONNECTIVITY DEVICE / NETWORK
Silicon Labs device (candidate)
Option A: SoC mode
Option B: NCP mode with host interface
Host link TBD
IP network + Matter ecosystem
Wi-Fi / Thread / Ethernet as applicable
BLE may be used for commissioning
Questions to resolve with the vendor and architecture owner
Exact part and mode? What host protocol and command interface? Who owns the network stack?
Is any internal switch IP actually customizable/licensable, or is the documented interface only a device host link?
Matter is not itself an on-chip crossbar and does not decide the CPU bus.
Reference: Silicon Labs Matter hardware requirements and SiWx917 documentation; see the linked research note for source URLs.
